contract.application_relevance: Workers parse textual attachments containing arbitrary marker-like strings.
contract.cleanup: Every case is awaited before cleanup. Track explicit readers and body streams; cancel/release readers, initiate all unlocked-stream cancellations before joining them, and retain no request-local objects. Buffered body producers may be lazy; explicit JS stream producers are finite and close synchronously. Cleanup records runtime-retained locks with awaited consumer/descendant proof, and any unverified lock blocks acceptance. No open producer gates, external handles or timers are used. Await both Y220 consumers with allSettled. If a body method or cleanup does not settle within the external deadline, supervisor terminates only the owned process group and records failure/unknown plus incomplete cleanup. It never reports a pass.
contract.desired_behavior: One notes.txt file contains prefix--MarkerLine-suffix followed by CRLF and second line.
contract.distinctness: Framing-position recognition, not binary decoding or malformed-boundary rejection.
fixed_runtime_assertions: t.equal([...form.keys()].length, 1, 'mid-line boundary-looking text does not create another part');
t.equal(await form.get('file').text(), 'prefix--MarkerLine-suffix\r\nsecond line', 'scanner recognizes delimiters only at line start');
t.equal(form.get('file').name, 'notes.txt', 'file metadata survives embedded marker text');
contract.hypothesis: A naive delimiter substring split may truncate valid file text that contains the boundary string in the middle of a line.
preconditions: Reviewed exact direct-celld source/build/deployment pins and fresh isolated local store.
Native celld Blob, File, FormData, Request, Response, and ReadableStream globals; no mocks or implementation extraction.
External five-second case deadline plus independent 300-second suite deadline and owned cleanup are active.

schedule.parallelism: two local body consumers joined with allSettled only in Y220; otherwise sequential

contract.source_observation: Pinned delimiter scan requires beginning-of-line placement. The body never places a conflicting delimiter prefix at line start.
